title: New nuclear builds, SMR developments in Canada, Turkey, Philippines, Thailand
summary: News from the international nuclear stage continues to flow at a steady pace, with recent happenings in Canada, Turkey, the Philippines, and Thailand. Here is the latest from Nuclear News’s international coverage.

title: Russia Begins Fuel Deliveries For First Load At Rooppur-2 Nuclear Plant
summary: Russia’s state-owned nuclear corporation Rosatom has begun delivering nuclear fuel for the initial loading of Unit 2 at Bangladesh’s Rooppur nuclear power station, a statement said. Rosatom said that it had completed a first shipment of fuel assemblies manufactured by its Novosibirsk Chemical Concentrates Plant in Russia. The fuel was transported to Bangladesh on a dedicated cargo flight. The company said the fuel containers had been transferred to a storage facility at Rooppur, where the assemblies undergo visual and technical inspections before they can be loaded into the reactor.

title: Nano Nuclear Signs MOU With Hyundai Engineering On US University Project
summary: Advanced nuclear energy and technology company Nano Nuclear Energy announced that it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Hyundai Engineering to establish a framework for potential collaboration to advance the Kronos MMR (micro-modular reactor) energy system project at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and to evaluate broader cooperation on future manufacturing and deployment. New York-based Nano said the MOU brings together its advanced reactor development programme with South Korea-based Hyundai Engineering capabilities including engineering, procurement, construction and project-management. The two companies initially intend to focus on areas including project-execution planning, conventional and site-related work, procurement readiness, supply-chain development and US localisation planning for the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign project.

title: NN asks: What is the role of online monitoring in plant maintenance?
summary: Adam Deatherage The role of online monitoring in plant maintenance is not simply to collect more data. It’s also to provide the information needed to make better maintenance decisions and more efficiently allocate critical craft resources. Historically, the nuclear industry has approached maintenance and surveillance testing activities on a calendar basis (quarterly, every outage, etc.). While this has been effective and straightforward to implement, 50-plus years of operating history has shown that many of these test intervals are overly conservative, resulting in what I’ve heard referred to as “recreational maintenance,” or maintenance activities that don’t actually add to the plant’s safety or reliability. Online monitoring enables a shift to condition-based maintenance, where real plant data can be used to demonstrate that surveillance can be extended and maintenance activities can be reduced. It also can provide early indication of component degradation.

title: Fusion companies sign LOIs for federal R&D awards
summary: The Department of Commerce announced the signing of four letters of intent for federal research and development awards under the CHIPS and Science Act focused on semiconductors and power electronics, including awards for fusion companies Helion and Commonwealth Fusion Systems.

title: US Agency Signs Agreement With Oil Company On Study Into SMRs For Turkey
summary: The US Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) has signed an agreement with Turkish oil refiner Tüpraş to fund a study into the potential use of small modular reactors (SMRs) to supply electricity, heat and steam for refinery operations. According to the USTDA, the proposed study will evaluate several US reactor technologies, including their technical and economic feasibility, environmental performance, regulatory requirements and potential industrial applications. The agreement is also expected to develop a roadmap to support Tüpraş in deciding whether to proceed with SMR deployment.

title: Power safely restored to Entergy Mississippi customers
summary: Entergy Mississippi has restored power to the customers in Lawrence County near Monticello, due to the wildfire in the area. Approximately 179 customers were originally taken offline as a proactive safety measure to help protect the public from wildfire hazards. Source

title: Entergy Mississippi responds to Lawrence County wildfire
summary: Entergy Mississippi has de-energized distribution lines that serve approximately 179 customers in Lawrence County near Monticello due to the spreading wildfire in the area. The temporary power outage is expected to last until approximately 7 p.m., though the outage could be extended until conditions are safe. Source

title: Entergy Louisiana launches $2 million bill credit program for eligible customers
summary: Entergy Louisiana is launching a $2 million bill assistance program to help residential customers manage higher household costs. Beginning Oct. 28 at 9 a.m., eligible customers can apply for a one-time $100 bill credit issued through their local United Way. Source
